key_insight: A readily available smartphone can provide low-cost mechanical excitation for ultrasound elastography, with preliminary phantom reconstructions similar to those obtained using a dedicated actuator.
engineering_relevance: Smartphone-based excitation could reduce equipment costs and integration complexity for tissue stiffness imaging.
method: Use a smartphone to induce mechanical excitation in a tissue-mimicking phantom.
Image the induced tissue displacements with ultrasound.
Solve the elasticity inverse problem using a finite element method.
evidence_signal: Preliminary phantom elasticity reconstructions were reported as similar to those using a dedicated actuator for harmonic excitation, without quantitative accuracy metrics in the abstract.
watch_item: Feasibility is demonstrated only in a phantom; excitation repeatability and performance in living tissue remain unestablished.
paper_title: Ultrasound Elastography: Excitation Methods and Low-Cost Alternative
